description: The filming workflow's example set (US-ME09, F5), in the marketingskills evals.json shape: each example's prompt, the output expected, its assertions, and its files. An example that carries `run` is re-run by the agent on every change to the filming Instructions (US-ME16, ADR 0003): its session writes the edit records its lab makes ready, in a throwaway lab built from `lab` and the example's own settings, with an approved filming plan, the post Drafts the example names, and footage made with ffmpeg's own test pattern to the facts files/footage.json gives each file the example names; its deterministic assertions are read off what the launcher took in and cut. An example's first file, if it has one, is checked by the unit tests (src/tests/test_filming_examples.py) against the synthetic kit in files/mandu, laid over the post-Draft example set's kit, and the synthetic footage inventory in files/footage.json; one that names what it needs runs only where the video tooling is installed, and is skipped with that reason elsewhere. A judged assertion is judged by nothing: the notice of a change lists it for the Founder. An edit example's files are its candidate edit record and its post Draft, then the reference leg's edit record and Draft when it is an A/B pair leg; an asset example's file holds the facts measured of a rendered asset.

assertion_kinds.deterministic: check is one of: plan_is_one_item; plan_films, plan_reuses, plan_on_camera, plan_unplanned (days); plan_sittings (count); plan_quotes_formats; edit_passes (with another leg's files: the two videos also show the same footage outside each one's opening); blocked_by (rule: a finding's rule; an example names every rule its record is blocked by); legs_not_offered (says: words of how the two legs' videos differ); asset_blocked (says: words of the finding); asset_kept; renders and legs_differ_only_in_the_opening (needs: video tooling); and, for a re-run example only: edit_passes and renders (day), no_edit (day), queued (item: a kind; count; cites: words each queued item holds), nothing_queued (item), nothing_set_aside
assertion_kinds.judged: text is a statement of the agent's output that no check decides; nothing judges it, and the notice of an Instructions change lists it as not judged

evals.prompt: Plan the filming of window 1 from the kit.
evals.expected_output: One filming plan item: every calendar day with an Angle has a shot list read from its Angle's Format, the later leg of each A/B pair adds no shot of its own, a re-cut leg whose Hook is said on camera is asked for its own opening take, and the shots fall into one sitting per setup the shot lists state.

assertions.text: Nothing in the plan says more about a shot than its Angle's Format and the calendar do.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1 (P01 / AB-1 leg A): the brief lists `window-1/d01-s1.mov`, 14.00s, for shot d01-s1, which may not be cut and runs in real time, and the Draft's beats end at 10s.
evals.expected_output: One segment: ten unbroken seconds of the one file, as recorded. It passes every check, and the launcher renders it as a 9:16 asset with the Draft's text drawn over it.

assertions.text: The agent chose its source range from the measured length alone, and said it could not see the footage.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 8 (P01 / AB-1 leg B), whose other leg, day 1, already has its video.
evals.expected_output: The same source ranges as day 1, from the first frame to the last: the legs share their footage, and only the Hook drawn over it differs.

assertions.text: The agent copied day 1's segments and changed nothing but the day.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 8; the candidate below starts its range a second later than day 1's.
evals.expected_output: The record passes its own checks, and the launcher does not offer the video cut from it: it and day 1's video do not show the same footage from the first frame to the last. Nothing changes for either leg, and the run report and a notice name the pair and what each video shows.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1; the candidate below drops two seconds from the middle of the recording.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it, naming the no-cut rule and its source: shot d01-s1 may not be cut, and the record shows it as two source ranges.

assertions.text: A good edit record of an uncut shot is one segment.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 2 (P02 / AB-3 leg A), whose shot list has a founder-on-camera shot and a screen recording; the candidate below shows only the founder.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it: shot d02-s2 has no footage in the edit, so there is no asset, and nothing is substituted for the shot.

assertions.text: When the brief lists no footage for a shot, the agent writes no edit record for the day and says which shot is missing.

evals.prompt: A rendered asset measures 1920x1080.
evals.expected_output: The launcher does not keep it: by measurement it is not 9:16.

evals.prompt: A rendered asset measures 720x1280.
evals.expected_output: The launcher does not keep it: it is 9:16, and not the expected 1080x1920.

evals.prompt: A rendered asset measures 1080x1920 at 30 frames a second, as long as its edit record.
evals.expected_output: The launcher keeps it.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1; the candidate below names a file in another folder by stepping out of the footage place.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it: an edit record can name only a file the footage place holds, so nothing outside the Founder's footage can enter a video.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1; the candidate below names a file by its full path elsewhere on the Mac.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it the same way.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1; the candidate below speeds the whole recording up to fit ten seconds.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it: the shot list says real time, so the recording plays only at the speed it was recorded at.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1; the candidate below runs twelve seconds.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it: the Format gives ten seconds, and the Draft's beats end at ten.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 7 (P07), a timelapse of a whole five-minute session: the brief lists `window-1/d07-s1.mov`, 330.00s.
evals.expected_output: One segment at twenty times the recorded speed: a timelapse is not real time, so its shot list lets it run faster. It passes.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 2 (P02 / AB-3 leg A), a pair whose opening the kit marks as re-cut: leg A's opening take, the screen recording, then the closing line.
evals.expected_output: Three segments, with leg A's own take in the opening. It passes.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 9 (P02 / AB-3 leg B), whose other leg, day 2, already has its video.
evals.expected_output: Leg B's own take in the opening, then the same source ranges as day 2. It passes: the legs differ only in the opening.

assertions.text: The agent used the take named for leg B in the opening and copied every later segment from day 2.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 9; the candidate below also starts the screen recording two seconds later than day 2's.
evals.expected_output: The record passes its own checks, and the launcher does not offer the video cut from it: it and day 2's video do not show the same footage after each one's opening. Nothing changes for either leg, and the run report and a notice name the pair and what each video shows.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 9; the candidate below opens on the take named for leg A.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks it: a take named for one leg is that leg's opening.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 1 and 7, both ready this run.
evals.expected_output: Two edit records that each pass every check and render: day 1 one unbroken range of its screen recording, day 7 the whole session sped up to the Draft's length.

assertions.text: The agent chose each source range from the measured facts alone, and said it could not see the footage.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 1 and 2; day 2's screen recording has not been filmed yet.
evals.expected_output: Day 1's edit record passes and renders; day 2 gets no edit record, since one of its shots has no footage.

assertions.text: The summary says day 2 waits on its screen recording, and writes nothing for it.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 1, 2, and 7, all ready this run.
evals.expected_output: Three edit records that each pass every check and render, each cut from its own day's footage.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 1 and 2; day 2's re-cut opening has only the take named for leg B.
evals.expected_output: Day 1's edit record passes; day 2 gets none, since leg A must open on a take of its own.

evals.prompt: Write the edit record for day 1, where an earlier run's record runs longer than the Draft and no longer passes.
evals.expected_output: The record rewritten to one unbroken range as long as the Draft's beats, which passes and renders.

assertions.text: A good edit record of an uncut shot is one segment.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 1 and 2, where day 2 has all its footage and no post Draft yet.
evals.expected_output: Day 1's edit record passes; day 2 gets none, since its text is drawn from a Draft that does not exist yet.

evals.prompt: Write the edit records for days 2 and 7: day 2 a re-cut pair leg with three shots, day 7 a five-minute timelapse.
evals.expected_output: Two edit records that pass every check and render: day 2 opening on leg A's own take, then the screen recording and the closing line; day 7 the whole session sped up to the Draft's length.

assertions.text: Day 2 opens on the take named for leg A, and every later segment is one a leg B record could copy unchanged.
